source: MIT 18.06 Linear Algebra, Lecture 1 (Gilbert Strang), ~34-42 min
keypoints: If the ninth column is the same as the eighth column, it contributes nothing new and some right-hand sides b become unreachable.
Nine columns and all their linear combinations may fill the whole nine-dimensional space.
With one redundant column, the combinations fill only an eight-dimensional plane inside nine-dimensional space.
The matrix form of a linear system is A times x equals b (a matrix A times a vector x equals a right-hand side b).
Matrix times vector, the column way: A times x is a linear combination of the columns of A.
Example: the matrix [[2,5],[1,3]] times the vector (1,2) equals (12, 7).
Matrix times vector, the row way: each component is a dot product of a row of A with x, e.g. 2*1 + 5*2 = 12.
If b = (12, 7) for that matrix, the correct solution is x = (1, 2).
Next lecture covers elimination: a systematic way to solve a system of any size and to detect when no solution exists.
